name: vision_fixmatch_bad
title: The same FixMatch run with nine planted defects
origin: domain-vision round 2: the dirty twin of vision_fixmatch. Its MLV301 is the label that shows --dataflow ip dropping a high-severity finding local reports (VIS2-05)

expected.why: nn.Module's _parameters / _modules dicts are never created, so the very first attribute assignment raises AttributeError

expected.defect: the residual blocks are held in a plain list comprehension
expected.why: none of them is registered, so they get no gradients, do not move with .to(device) and are absent from every state_dict - the network trains its first and last layer only
every BatchNorm2d in the WideResNet updates its running statistics from the validation split, so the statistics the next epoch trains with were learned on data the model is scored against
expected.gap: local reports this at high / 0.85; --dataflow ip drops it entirely, with no diagnostic. Minimal 38-line repro in the round-2 report (VIS2-05).

expected.defect: both running totals keep the live loss tensors
expected.why: every batch's autograd graph is retained for the whole epoch, and a FixMatch step holds three forward passes worth of graph
the graph for the whole validation set is built twice per epoch - once for the student, once for the shadow - and discarded
expected.gap: same as MLV301: local reports it, --dataflow ip does not (VIS2-05).

expected.defect: the unlabelled loader does not shuffle
expected.why: the pool is stored in class order, so every unlabelled batch is one class; the confidence mask then selects that class and the pseudo-label distribution collapses onto it
expected.gap: MLV110 needs the dataset to carry TRAIN_SPLIT or the loader name to match (?i)train_?(loader|dl). An unlabelled pool is neither - `unlabelled_loader` is a training loader by role and by no other signal, and the loop that consumes it does so through next(iter(...)) rather than a for statement, so the backward() clause cannot reach it either.

expected.defect: the validation split is read through the strong (RandAugment + RandomErasing) pipeline
expected.why: the reported accuracy is measured on images the model was never meant to see at test time, and it moves by several points between runs for that reason alone
expected.gap: MLV114 requires the dataset construction to resolve to a knowledge-table DATASET row; ImageListDataset is a workspace Dataset subclass. See VIS2-01.

expected.why: the student and the shadow are scored on two different orderings of the same split, so the two accuracies printed side by side are not comparable batch for batch

expected.defect: nothing is seeded and the label subset is drawn from an unseeded generator
expected.why: the 25-labels-per-class benchmark is a different benchmark on every run, which is the one thing a semi-supervised result has to hold fixed

expected.defect: the EMA shadow is updated before optimizer.step() instead of after
expected.why: the shadow averages the weights the student is about to leave rather than the ones it reaches, so it lags the student by one step forever and the 'EMA accuracy' that is checkpointed is not the quantity the paper reports
expected.gap: MLV203 is the nearest rule - it is about an ordering defect inside one training step - but it only compares OPT_STEP against BACKWARD. No rule models the EMA protocol.

expected.defect: the pseudo-label and the confidence mask are read off the strong view instead of the weak one
expected.why: FixMatch's premise is that the weakly augmented view is the reliable teacher; taking both the label and the confidence from the RandAugment-ed view makes the model its own noisy teacher, and training collapses to whichever class the mask first admits
expected.gap: no rule models the two-view consistency protocol. MLV305 is the nearest code (a metric or a decision taken from the wrong tensor) but it is written for sklearn / torchmetrics class metrics.

forbidden.why: same trap as the clean twin, and it fires: LambdaLR has no intrinsic cadence and this one is built over epochs * len(labelled_loader) steps, so stepping it per batch is correct. Round-2 finding VIS2-04
there is no sklearn transformer in this project
nothing is fitted on anything here
the loaders are built inside build_loaders(), reached only from main() under the __main__ guard
optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) is still the first statement of the training step
optimizer.step() is still called every batch
loss.backward() at line 130 is outside the no_grad pseudo-label block; ModelEMA.update is decorated @torch.no_grad() and contains no backward()
there is no gradient clipping in this project
no ranking metric is computed anywhere
the softmax at line 123 stays inside the no_grad block and never reaches F.cross_entropy, which is fed logits directly
there is no sigmoid and no BCE loss in this project
the model and the shadow are both moved with .to(device) and every batch tensor is moved inside the loop
there is no sklearn split and no random_split; the unseeded draw is labelled as MLV601 above
the checkpoint still saves state_dict()s, never the modules

gaps.what: no rule models the EMA/shadow-model protocol: update after the optimizer step, decay applied to parameters and a straight copy for buffers, and the shadow evaluated rather than trained
gaps.evidence: train.py:133 against the clean twin's line 135

gaps.what: no rule models the two-view consistency protocol, so reading the pseudo-label off the strong view - the single most damaging FixMatch bug - is invisible
gaps.evidence: train.py:123 against the clean twin's logits_weak

unsupported.why: LABEL CORRECTED in hardening round 2: MLV703 is not a built rule - it carries the status **later** in docs/ISSUE_RULES.md section 1 - so a label for it can never be satisfied and can never be violated. `analyzer/tests/accuracy/test_accuracy.py::test_every_labelled_code_is_a_real_rule` rejects one, and this row turned that shipped test red. The observation is kept verbatim here so the row can be restored the day the rule ships. Original verdict `forbidden`, original note: F.dropout still passes training=self.training
